T1.pun: LA PORTE TOURNE SUR LE GOND · LE GOND TOURNE SUR LA PORTE
T1.gloss_en: The door turns on the hinge / the hinge turns on the door. 'Tourner' is also 'to shoot a film': the door is filming its hinge, the hinge its door; and 'sortir de ses gonds' (to come off the hinge) is to lose one's temper. On a turning disc, what is the pivot and what is the thing that turns is exactly what the chiasmus swaps.

T2.pun: LA CLOCHE DU QUAI SONNE LA CLEF · LA CLEF DU QUAI SONNE LA CLOCHE
T2.gloss_en: The platform bell rings the key / the platform key rings the bell. 'Clef' is both the key that opens and the musical clef or key-note: the bell 'sounds the key' (gives the pitch), and the key 'rings the bell' (rings for the train, opens the bell-tower). Slang 'ca cloche' = 'something is off'. The two nouns change places and the station keeps the same hour.

T1.slide_note: one continuous Archimedean spiral (turn pitch = TEXT_PITCH_RINGS x ring pitch); glyph i corresponds to ring c(i) = the ring nearest its radius (order-preserving: c is non-decreasing in i), so its radial slide onto ring c(i) is at most half a pitch = one ring band. The geometric turn index ('turn') runs ahead of 'ring' by the rim offset (the outer turn starts 1.2 px inside ring 0's radius, a limit set by the 232 px rim that the letter tops must stay inside).

reading_speed.chosen_omega_read: 1/128 rev/frame = 2.8125 deg/frame = 0.1875 rev/s (67.5 deg/s); integer period P = 128 frames
reading_speed.chosen_interval: 7.0 s = 168 frames starting at F288 (plan had 5.75 s at 1/256); T2 first token phase-locked to 12 o-clock on screen at the interval start (glyphs.PHASE["T2"] = theta(F288))
reading_speed.recommendation_to_director_and_U3: Replace omega_read 1/256 by 1/128 and lengthen the declared reading interval to 168 frames (F288-455), shifting W3/O_B/still pass by +30 frames, or take the 30 frames from O_B. I5 then asserts P = 128. If the 5.75 s interval must be kept, 1/128 still reads at a fluent 13 chars/s but the last two letters tilt past 110 deg.
justification: Structural (reading model, measured): the disc turns ccw, so a reader holding the 12 o-clock point is FED the text in token order. At 1/128 the outer turn passes 12 o-clock at 9.9 chars/s, which is a deliberate reading-aloud pace (10 chars/s); the reading point therefore stays near the top and every letter of the 65-char pun is read with tilt <= 38 deg (10 chars/s) or <= 84 deg (13 chars/s). Zero inverted letters.

At 1/256 (plan) and 1/384 the plate feeds only 5.0 and 3.3 chars/s, so the reader must run ahead clockwise round the plate and reaches the inverted 4-8 o-clock sector: 15-19 inverted letters, the reading position is lost in the second half around "LA CLEF DU QUAI" (A, 13 chars/s) and "SONNE LA CL.." (B). At 10 chars/s the 6.5 s reading does not even fit the 5.75 s interval.

Longer exposure at 1/256 (8.0 s, variant C): the time fits but the geometry does not: 9-19 letters still pass through the inverted sector; lost near "LA CLEF DU QUAI" (the turn-0 to turn-1 wrap of the second half). Slower is NOT easier on a turning spiral: it is the feed rate at 12 o-clock that matters.

Sweep (simulated only, not rendered): feasible band 1/96..1/144 at 7 s; 1/80 inverts at 10 chars/s and blurs 8 px; 1/128 is the slowest speed in the band that keeps 13 chars/s readable and is an integer period.

Perceptually judged (my own frame-by-frame look at 960x540 and 2x crops of the rendered clips, not a live normal-speed viewing by an independent person): at 1/128 the outer letters carry a 5 px tangential shutter smear against a 3.9 px stroke; still clearly legible, softer than 1/256 (2.6 px), and it reads as the 1926 softness coming from real rotation. Reading position is most at risk at the turn-0 -> turn-1 wrap inside "QUAI | SONNE" of the second half (the eye must drop one turn inward); the separator dot before each half is the re-anchor point. The independent reviewer must confirm by reading T2 aloud at normal speed.

where_position_is_lost.A 1/256 5.75 s: 10 chars/s: does not fit; 13 chars/s: lost at letter ~7 of the second half ("..LA CLEF|L.."), 15-19 inverted letters
where_position_is_lost.B 1/384 5.75 s: 10 chars/s: does not fit; 13 chars/s: lost in "..SONNE LA CL.." of the second half, 16-17 inverted letters
where_position_is_lost.C 1/256 8.0 s: 10 chars/s: lost at "..CLEF DU QUAI" (second half, 10-19 inverted); 13 chars/s: lost at "DU QUAI" (9-17 inverted)

results.theta_source: placeholder: F24-263 at 1/80 + 24-frame ease to 1/256 (score.json absent)
results.model:
(structural; the perceptual part is my own frame-by-frame look, labelled as such):
  a reader reads the T2 disc aloud at rho chars/s, token after token along the GlyphPath, starting at a
  half-separator of their choosing at a time of their choosing inside the declared reading interval;
  a token read at time t sits at screen angle a = phi_i - theta(t) (image coords, cw positive), and its
  letter's 'up' is the outward normal, so its tilt from upright is a + 90 deg.
  |tilt| <= 60: upright; 60-110: rotated, readable with effort; > 110: inverted = reading position lost.

absences: No foraged material is used or needed by this unit (handmade type and plate; no downloads). The reference spiralTextPom.webp is used only side by side for measurement/comparison, never composited.
No openly licensed recording of the puns read aloud exists (they are original); voice stays as the on-screen disc, no captions.

handmade.what: Two original French chiasmus puns T1, T2 with English glosses; checked against the ten Duchamp Anemic cinema disc texts (no phrase match, no shared word 3-gram)

GlyphPath layout: inward clockwise Archimedean spiral, tops out, LiberationSans-Bold caps 24.5 px (1x), turn pitch 42 px = 1.4 O_A ring pitches, pitch/cap 1.716 (kf-2 1.467, opened 17 %), tracking 1.19-1.32x, spacing held at the letter inner edge

Text-disc renderer: neutral sphere-lit plate (L 221/204 top-left -> 58 bottom-right), letters L 232 median cut from the 2.5 px groove stock (+-3 %), 1.5 px emboss shadow from camera-fixed upper-left light, 2x supersampling, 8-sub-frame 180-degree shutter, no grain
